children: China's piecemeal stimulus measures remain insufficient relative to the pace of domestic demand weakening, say BofA Global Research economists in a note. However, some recent policies could weigh on growth, at least in the near term, they say. New property policies curbing the presale model, under which developers could sell homes before units are ready for delivery, may hurt new housing starts and investment next year, which would also weigh on local governments' revenue from land sales and overall growth. A credible policy pivot combining stronger fiscal support, more decisive monetary easing and measures to boost consumption and investment, is needed to reverse expectations and support a durable recovery in domestic demand, BofA says. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
